reason: Records are synthetic and incomplete: of 4 expected run cells, 3 completed and 1 (eval-b/without_skill/run-1) errored with no grading. The two configurations are therefore not comparable as groups (without_skill coverage 0.50 vs with_skill 1.00). Only 1 of 2 planned eval_id x run pairs is valid, so no averaged or overall delta can be formed. The one computable difference (eval-a pass_rate 1.0 vs 0.0) is synthetic and n=1 and cannot support a claim about overall skill gain.

eval-a.caveat: synthetic, n=1, not a real measurement

overall.reason: 1/2 valid pairs; missing cell not imputable

limitations: All input records are synthetic fixtures; they do not measure real model behavior.
Only one iteration and n=1 run per eval/configuration: no variance, no statistical inference.
One of four cells errored (eval-b/without_skill) and produced no grading; excluding it would bias any comparison.
Only 1 of 2 planned pairs is valid; the two configurations have unequal completion (coverage 1.00 vs 0.50), so they are not comparable.
Token and cost measurements were not supplied and are reported as null, never as zero.
No skill-provided benchmark tool was present in the workspace; aggregation was done with the Python standard library.
evidence_boundary: Conclusions are limited to a faithful transcription of the synthetic fixtures and an inventory of their gaps. No claim can be made that the skill improves real task performance, reduces latency, or changes cost.
